solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Countermand second set of changes?

definitions.meaning: to ... an order or law is to revoke or countermand it
read as ..., a peal (a set of changes rung on bells) done again

explanation.surface: Someone cancels an order for a second round of alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: In bell-ringing a 'change' is one sequence of the bells and a peal is a long set of them, so a second peal is a re-peal.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law or instruction is to revoke it, which is what countermanding does.

clue.text: Socialist stalwart of certain universities?

parts.note: red is the traditional colour, and hence nickname, of a socialist
a brick is an informal word for a reliable, loyal person, a stalwart

explanation.surface: A left-wing loyalist at some universities.
explanation.walkthrough: Redbrick universities are the British civic universities founded in industrial cities around 1900, named for their brick buildings, as distinct from Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbrick is an adjective applied to a group of later British universities, contrasted with the ancient colleges.

clue.text: What's exclaimed when striking inmate in conflict

definitions.meaning: the comic-book exclamation for a punch landing
a prisoner of war, held captive during a conflict

explanation.definitionFit: Pow is an interjection for a blow, and POW abbreviates prisoner of war, a captive taken in fighting.

clue.text: Outlaw historically needing to gain time

parts.note: to attain something is to gain or achieve it

explanation.surface: An old-time bandit who needs time to make his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Historically' marks an obsolete sense: in old law to attaint someone was to strip them of civil rights after a conviction for treason or felony.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainting a person in old English law made them effectively an outlaw, with property and rights forfeited.

clue.text: Rush bedding that should keep camper drier

parts.note: to fly is to rush or hurry
a sheet is a piece of bedding

explanation.surface: Hurried bedding meant to keep someone sleeping under canvas dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush bedding' suggests reeds strewn for sleeping on, but rush is the verb fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A flysheet is the outer waterproof layer pitched over a tent to keep the occupants dry.

clue.text: Doctor foretold extremes of Holmes' life in novel

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from Holmes

explanation.surface: Doctor Watson predicted how Sherlock Holmes's life would turn out, in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' next to Holmes makes you think of Watson. It is really the anagram signal, and 'novel' is both the definition and part of the story the surface tells.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord of the Flies is William Golding's 1954 novel about stranded schoolboys.

clue.text: Music beloved of the French, with variable piercing note

indicators.note: one piece piercing another goes through the middle of it

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
cher is French for dear or beloved
Z is a letter used for a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: French love song with a changing, piercing tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively movement or piece of music, often the third in a symphony.

clue.text: Man of property, possibly China's James Bond?

parts.note: China is an example of an E (Eastern) state, giving E + STATE
James Bond is the fictional secret agent 007

explanation.surface: A Chinese spy figure asked about as a property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: China, as one example, is an Eastern state, so the Chinese James Bond would be an E state agent.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent deals in houses and land, so is in the property business.

clue.text: The latest goal in test

indicators.note: the goal is placed in the test, one word inside the other

parts.note: to try something is to test it
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A newest scoring attempt during a match, perhaps in Test cricket or rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Goal, try and test all point to sport, but each is a plain synonym here.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, in line with the latest style.

clue.text: Journalist leading session in sweeper's compact quarters

indicators.note: the two pieces are put inside the sweeper's word

parts.note: a broom is a sweeper

indicators.note: the journalist leads, coming before the session

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist
a sitting is a session, as of a court or parliament

explanation.surface: A reporter heads a meeting held in a cleaner's cramped lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed-sitting room is a single rented room used for both sleeping and living, a compact form of lodging.

clue.text: Sensible planet's responsibility?

definitions.meaning: if something is ..., it is the planet Earth's job

explanation.definitionFit: A down-to-earth person is practical and realistic; 'down to' someone also means their responsibility.

clue.text: Regularly removed attire?

indicators.note: letters taken out at regular intervals from attire, every other one

explanation.surface: Clothing that is routinely taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth and sixth letters of attire are drawn out, and the result is itself an item of attire often removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a piece of clothing, frequently the first item loosened and taken off.

clue.text: Boxer's reported range

indicators.note: reported means as heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: Rocky Balboa is the boxer in the Rocky films, and also Rocky Marciano

explanation.surface: How far the boxer was said to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a boxer's reach, but it is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rockies are the great mountain range of western North America.

clue.text: Priest cries out loud for ammunition

indicators.note: out loud means the words are spoken, giving their sound

parts.note: a canon is a priest attached to a cathedral, and bawls means cries loudly

explanation.surface: A clergyman shouts for weapons supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannonballs are the round shot fired from old cannons, a form of ammunition.

clue.text: CGS unit formerly included in dictionary

indicators.note: one piece is included inside another

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
erst is an archaic word for formerly

explanation.surface: A unit of the old centimetre-gram-second system once listed in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is the CGS unit of magnetic field strength, named after the physicist Hans Christian Oersted.

clue.text: Authorised airing, just what the doctor ordered?

definitions.meaning: sanctioned by or in line with a constitution

definitions.text: airing, just what the doctor ordered?
definitions.meaning: a walk taken for one's health, an airing

explanation.definitionFit: Constitutional describes what a constitution permits; as a noun it is a health-giving stroll.

clue.text: Small fly found in child's trifle

indicators.note: the fly is found inside the child

parts.note: a son is a child
a midge is a tiny fly

explanation.surface: A tiny insect discovered in a youngster's dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' looks like the pudding but means a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a very small amount, a trifle.

clue.text: Male radio geek's broadcast runs flawlessly

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's amateur radio transmission works perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes like a dream operates smoothly, with no problems at all.

clue.text: Some people primarily colder or hotter?

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letters of the words before

parts.note: icier means colder

explanation.surface: Whether some people are mainly cold or hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Colder and hotter look like a pair of opposites, but one is wordplay and the other the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicier food is more strongly seasoned, so hotter to the taste.

clue.text: Double trouble for plant

parts.note: to dog someone is to shadow or tail them, as a double follows a person
a bane is a source of trouble

explanation.surface: Twice the problems for a factory or garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogbane is a plant, once thought poisonous to dogs.

clue.text: Rising whale and youngster emerge

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the orca, or orc, is the killer whale
a pup is a young animal

explanation.surface: A whale and its calf surface from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop up is to appear unexpectedly, to emerge.

clue.text: Abrasive pair of bachelors feeling sorry for nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one word holds the other

parts.note: ruing means regretting, feeling sorry
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, so two give BB

explanation.surface: Two unmarried men, harsh and full of regret for the carers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like a noun but is the verb holding the bachelors.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing is wearing away by friction, which is what an abrasive action does.

clue.text: Tied up, held in college perhaps on large island

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the college word follows the large island

parts.note: at Oxford and Cambridge a gated student is confined to college as a punishment

explanation.surface: Someone bound and confined at a college on a big island.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'gated' is a British university punishment: confinement to college after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligated means bound with a ligature, as a surgeon ties off a blood vessel.

clue.text: Comrade's drink knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A friend's glass is spilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is a friend or mate, a comrade.

clue.text: Ineffectual vocal work almost stops popular musical returning

indicators.note: the shortened opera stops up a gap between the other pieces

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: returning means the musical's name is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an opera is a sung dramatic work

explanation.surface: A weak opera nearly halts a hit show coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón. 'Stops' is the containment signal: the shortened opera plugs the gap between the other pieces, the way a stopper fills a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Inoperative means not working or having no effect, so ineffectual.

clue.text: Harmful tablet, quietly disposed of

indicators.note: disposed of means that letter is thrown away

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
P, for piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A dangerous pill is discreetly thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as an adjective can mean bad or harmful, as in ill effects.

clue.text: Smoked meat I added to previous stuff

indicators.note: the I is added on to the end of the other pieces

parts.note: past means previous or former
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A cook adds ingredients to leftovers with some cured beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned smoked beef, a deli staple.

clue.text: Joined the line and collapsed

definitions.meaning: soldiers fall in when they form ranks
a roof that falls in collapses

explanation.definitionFit: Fell in is both the past of fall in, getting into formation, and of caving inwards.
